incident: Synnovis (NHS south east London pathology provider) ransomware attack by Qilin, 3 June 2024

sources.title: NHS England - Synnovis cyber attack: statement from NHS England (June 2024)
sources.what_it_gave: attack date 3 June, ransomware on Synnovis, blood-testing systems unusable, samples discarded, encrypted backup copy of results held, NCSC/NCA verifying published data

sources.title: NHS England London - Update on cyber incident: clinical impact in south east London, Thursday 25 July 2024
sources.what_it_gave: attack started Monday 3 June; cumulative 1,608 elective procedures and 8,349 outpatient appointments postponed; NHSBT Amber Alert on O-type blood; blood transfusion restoration expected early autumn; core chemistry and haematology systems rebuilt; pathology capacity 60%

sources.title: NHS England London - Update on cyber incident: clinical impact in south east London, Thursday 26 September 2024
sources.what_it_gave: cumulative 10,152 acute outpatient appointments and 1,710 elective procedures postponed at KCH and GSTT; GP pathology returned; blood transfusion service still being restored; HR/procurement administrative systems next

sources.title: NHS England London - statement on Synnovis ransomware cyber attack, 5 June 2024
sources.what_it_gave: affected trusts (GSTT, KCH, SE London primary care), postponed operations and phlebotomy, NHS England cyber incident response team deployed

sources.title: UK Parliament written ministerial statement (Cyber Security and Resilience Bill) referencing Synnovis
sources.what_it_gave: 'computer systems were hacked, private patient data was stolen, and IT systems were rendered useless'; five trusts disrupted; over 11,000 appointments delayed; contributed to a patient death; Synnovis estimated financial impact GBP 32.7m

sources.title: HSJ via Patient Safety Learning hub - 'Basic security measure would have prevented disastrous cyber attack' (27 Sep 2024)
sources.what_it_gave: senior response sources: the affected system had no multi-factor authentication; NHS England CISO Phil Huggins then mandated 2FA for all NHS and supplier systems; system itself not named

sources.title: Digital Health - 'Two-factor authentication may have stopped Synnovis cyber attack' (Sep 2024)
sources.what_it_gave: NHS England's Beverley Bryant: attack 'may not have happened' with 2FA; no entry system named

sources.title: TechRadar - Russia-linked Qilin group says it was responsible for London hospitals cyberattack (19 Jun 2024)
sources.what_it_gave: Qilin's unverified claim (via Bloomberg) that it 'abused a zero day exploit'; USD 50m demand; Synnovis working with NCSC

sources.title: Bitdefender Hot for Security - Patient death linked to cyberattack on British pathology clinic Synnovis
sources.what_it_gave: KCH safety investigation: 'a long wait for a blood test result due to the cyber-attack' was a contributing factor; 400 GB published; ~900,000 records estimated

narrative_before: On Monday 3 June 2024 Synnovis, the pathology provider for Guy's and St Thomas' and King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trusts and south east London GPs, was hit by Qilin ransomware; its IT systems were 'rendered useless' and patient data stolen (UK Parliament written statement). Blood-testing and blood-transfusion matching could not run, so hospitals reverted to paper, prioritised only urgent tests and relied on mutual aid; NHS Blood and Transplant issued an Amber Alert restricting O-type blood and appealed for O-negative and O-positive donors (NHS England 25 July update). By 16-22 September 10,152 acute outpatient appointments and 1,710 elective procedures had been postponed at the two trusts (NHS England 26 September update); the ministerial statement puts total delays above 11,000 and Synnovis's own financial impact at GBP 32.7m. Qilin demanded USD 50m and, when unpaid, published about 400 GB of data (TechRadar; Bitdefender). A King's College Hospital safety investigation later found that a long wait for a blood test result caused by the attack contributed to a patient's death (Bitdefender). Synnovis rebuilt substantial parts of its IT estate; core chemistry and haematology returned over the summer and blood transfusion by early autumn, with HR and procurement systems restored last (NHS England 25 July and 26 September updates).

detection_moments.description: Monday 3 June 2024: Synnovis discovers that its pathology IT systems are encrypted; blood testing and transfusion systems cannot be used and the attack is already at the impact stage (T1486). No earlier detection moment is public.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the cause was a ransomware attack on pathology provider Synnovis, starting Monday 3 June' (NHS England London update, 25 July 2024); 'IT systems were rendered useless' (UK Parliament written statement)

ambiguities: No public source names the entry point. HSJ (via PSL hub) reports only that 'the affected system' lacked MFA, without naming it; Qilin's claim of a 'zero day exploit' (TechRadar/Bloomberg) is unverified and names no product.
No public source describes any lateral movement hop inside Synnovis; therefore links and attack_path are empty and the incident is dropped per the brief.

The machine list (LIMS, blood transfusion system, admin systems) is inferred from the services NHS England says were lost and restored ('core chemistry and haematology', 'blood transfusion', 'HR and procurement'); no hostnames, server counts, domain controllers or workstations are public.
Redundancy: no source says these systems had replicas, so replicas=1. depends_on left empty because no dependency is documented.
The 400 GB / ~900,000-record figures for stolen data are from the attackers' leak and third-party estimates, not an official count.
NHS England 'lessons learned' material is not published beyond the MFA mandate letter reported by HSJ; the Hansard/written statement gives impact only.
drop_reason: Public sources (NHS England statements, Parliament written statement, HSJ, Qilin's own claims) give the impact and detection date but neither the entry point nor a single lateral hop; the brief requires both.
